root_idea.summary: The root centers on spreading, extending, and laying something out.
root_idea.development: From physical spreading and extension, Classical usage develops related senses of being carried away or propelled, lying extended on the ground, and describing expansive or numerous formations.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested Form I verb and is displayed under its normalized dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To spread or extend outward; in the Quranic occurrence, to spread out the earth.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive in the attested verse, with the earth as object. The Quranic spelling is طَحَىٰ in the supplied occurrence; طَحَا and طَحَى are reported as dialectal variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repel or push one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or mutual use applied to a people or party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become spread, extended, or stretched; to throw or prostrate someone face-down, to lie stretched on the ground, or to stick to the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes intransitive physical-state uses and constructions describing a person, a camel, or someone lying or sleeping extended on the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away into the land; to carry or drive someone or something away, or propel it onward; figuratively, to carry a person into pursuit or a far-reaching course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes uses of the heart or anxiety carrying someone away, and the transitive expression for throwing a ball.
Attested in a phrase describing a person's fatness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become distant or remote.
The lower, baser, or basest of mankind or the people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributed and apparently uncertain lexical usage, reported with the spelling طَحَى.
A nominal designation; the closely resembling form طَخْيَةٌ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Spread out, expansive, or filling everything by its multitude; applied to an army or to a great spreading tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing extensive spread or abundance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vultures circling in the sky around the bodies of the slain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional plural expression describing circling vultures.
Attested in the oath-expression “by the high moon.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great congregated body of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominalized or substantivized use referring to a large assembled multitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Spread, expanded, or extended; thrown face-down or lying and stretching face-down on the ground, and cleaving or sticking to it; of a plant, spreading over the surface of the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival derived-form usage covering both prone or ground-adhering subjects and vegetation spreading along the ground.
